# CFOLogic

> CFOLogic is a full-stack finance partner for growth-focused businesses ($2-50M revenue): fractional CFO strategy, FP&A, controllership and finance operations (FinOps), delivered by senior finance leaders in the US backed by a 40+ person Center of Excellence in Pune, India. Services include CEO Navigator™ (full finance function for founder-led businesses), CFO Success Partners™ (execution capacity for sitting CFOs), Smart Dashboards, deal support, and white-label CAS capacity for CPA firms.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://cfologic.com/): Full-stack finance - CFO strategy, FP&A, controller and finance operations from one team
- [Finance Team as a Service](https://cfologic.com/finance-team-as-a-service): What FTaaS is, the four layers (FinOps, controller, FP&A, fractional CFO), the hybridshore delivery model (US-based leadership, India-based teams, high AI leverage), and a costed comparison against hiring in-house
- [For Founders & CEOs](https://cfologic.com/founders): CEO Navigator™ - the full finance pyramid as a service
- [For CFOs](https://cfologic.com/cfo-success-partners): CFO Success Partners™ - retained execution team for finance leaders
- [For CFO/CAS Firms](https://cfologic.com/accounting-firms): HybridShore capability for US CFO/CAS firms
- [For Acquisition Entrepreneurs](https://cfologic.com/acquisition-entrepreneurs): Diligence and deal support before the close; lender-ready finance, covenant and DSCR monitoring after
- [For Capital Providers](https://cfologic.com/capital-providers): Portfolio-wide Navigator reporting and an on-call CFO Success Partners™ bench for private credit funds, PE and search investors, and independent sponsors
- [Case Studies](https://cfologic.com/case-studies)
- [About](https://cfologic.com/about)
- [Trust Center](https://cfologic.com/trust-center): Security and data handling

## Insights (blog)
- [Accounts Payable After an Acquisition: What to Fix First](https://cfologic.com/insights/accounts-payable-after-an-acquisition/): What a new owner should do with accounts payable in the first weeks after closing — listing every open bill, separating the seller's period, verifying vendor bank details, setting approval rules and a payment rhythm, telling vendors about the change of ownership, and automating once the basics hold.
- [Year-End Close for 2026: What Changes, Including the $2,000 1099 Threshold](https://cfologic.com/insights/year-end-close-2026-1099-threshold/): A year-end close checklist for 2026 for founder-led businesses — the new $2,000 Form 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC threshold and its exceptions, the 1099-K threshold, W-9 collection, reconciliations, receivables, inventory, accruals, payroll year-end, deadlines in early 2027 and what to hand to the CPA.
- [Your First Real Annual Budget: Building FY2027 for a $3–10M Services Business](https://cfologic.com/insights/first-annual-budget-fy2027-services-business/): A step-by-step approach to a first annual budget for a services business — revenue from clients and pipeline, capacity from headcount and utilization, the hiring plan, overhead, a monthly cash budget, a downside case, and the monthly review that makes the budget useful.
- [Job Costing After an Acquisition: Finding Out Which Customers Make Money](https://cfologic.com/insights/job-costing-after-an-acquisition/): How a new owner can find customer and job profitability in a service business that never tracked it — the costs that get missed, a rough first cut by segment, tying spend and labor to jobs, and what to do with customers who cost more than they pay.
- [Profit First or a Cash Forecast? What Each One Tells an Owner](https://cfologic.com/insights/profit-first-vs-cash-flow-forecast/): How the Profit First cash management method works, what it does well, where it falls short for growing businesses, how a forward cash forecast differs, and how to use the two together so cash discipline does not create timing shortfalls.
- [Plan Working Capital Around the Peak, Not the Average](https://cfologic.com/insights/working-capital-at-its-peak/): Why a small business's working capital need changes through the month, how billing, payroll and supplier terms create a peak, how to find yours, and how to plan cash, credit lines and account transfers around it rather than the average.
- [Your Books After a Stock Purchase: Recording the Deal Before the CPA Asks](https://cfologic.com/insights/books-after-a-stock-purchase/): What a buyer must record in the acquired company's books after a stock purchase — the funds flow at closing, debt payoffs, transaction costs, payouts, the new financing, the holding company relationship and the cut-off at the closing date — and why to line up the accountant before closing.
- [ROIC, Not Revenue: Deciding Where the Next Dollar Goes Across Locations](https://cfologic.com/insights/roic-not-revenue-multi-location/): Why multi-location owners should compare return on invested capital rather than revenue when deciding where to invest, how to measure it per location, why returns fall as a location approaches its revenue ceiling, and how higher-cost markets change the picture.
- [The 90-Day Working Capital True-Up: What It Involves and Why It Takes So Long](https://cfologic.com/insights/90-day-working-capital-true-up/): What happens in the post-closing working capital true-up — the cut-off of bills, receivables, work in progress and payroll at the closing date, bad debts, the recalculation against the peg, how the result is settled — and how to prepare so it does not consume the buyer's first quarter.
- [Getting Your Financials Deal-Ready: What Buyers and Lenders Look For](https://cfologic.com/insights/getting-your-financials-deal-ready/): A seller's guide to deal-ready financials — what buyers and lenders actually test, what SBA lenders now require under SOP 50 10 8.1, the statements and schedules to prepare, the issues that slow diligence, whether to commission a sell-side quality of earnings, and a timeline from two years out to the data room.
- [The Questions Clients Ask Between Monthly Meetings, and Who Answers Them](https://cfologic.com/insights/client-questions-between-monthly-meetings-cas/): Why CAS clients ask most of their questions between monthly meetings, what those questions cost a firm in unbilled senior time, the options for handling them — absorb, scope, schedule or self-serve — and how to keep answers consistent with the numbers the firm closed.
- [An Outsourced Bookkeeper and an In-House One: When to Consolidate Into One Finance Team](https://cfologic.com/insights/consolidating-outsourced-and-in-house-bookkeeper/): Why growing companies end up with split bookkeeping between an outside firm and an in-house person, the signs it has stopped working, the three ways to consolidate, and how to handle the transition fairly for the people involved.
- [AI in Buy-Side Due Diligence: What It Can Check and What It Cannot](https://cfologic.com/insights/ai-in-buy-side-due-diligence/): Where AI genuinely helps in buy-side due diligence on a small business — reading contracts and ledgers at volume, flagging anomalies, comparing records — where it fails, how to handle the seller's confidential data, and how to make AI findings something a lender or partner can rely on.
- [Allocating Head-Office Costs Across a Multi-Property Hotel Group](https://cfologic.com/insights/allocating-head-office-costs-multi-property-hotel-group/): How a multi-property hotel group can separate head-office costs from property operations, choose allocation methods that hold up, charge them through a management fee or intercompany entries, and read property results before and after allocation.
- [Project Accounting in QuickBooks Online for Time-and-Materials Services Firms](https://cfologic.com/insights/project-accounting-quickbooks-online-time-and-materials/): How a time-and-materials services firm can set up project accounting in QuickBooks Online — customer and project structure, service items and rates, time and billable expenses, invoicing from approved time, unbilled work at month end, retainers and caps — and what to keep outside QuickBooks.
- [Customer Concentration in an Acquisition: How Lenders Read It and How Deals Get Structured](https://cfologic.com/insights/customer-concentration-acquisition-lenders/): How customer concentration affects a small business acquisition — how to measure it beyond a single percentage, how lenders read it against debt service coverage, the structures that share the risk between buyer and seller, and how to test the covenant model before the credit agreement is signed.
- [Bookkeeping for HVAC Companies: The Numbers an Owner in the Field Needs](https://cfologic.com/insights/bookkeeping-for-hvac-companies/): How to set up and run bookkeeping for an HVAC company — job costing for installs and service calls, maintenance agreements as deferred revenue, inventory on trucks, technician pay and commissions, seasonal cash and receivables — and the handful of numbers an owner should see every week.
